mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of periods when the federal funds rate declines by at least 0.25% over 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tight labor market that increases the risk of inflation-driven monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a low federal funds rate signal robust economic demand and accommodative monetary policy, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term (HOUST * FEDFUNDS) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below its 12-month moving average during a late-cycle contraction signals weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods classified as late-cycle contraction, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of periods when housing starts rise by at least 1% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI above 2.5% signals elevated inflation that increases the probability of monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% YoY, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment and retail sales signals robust consumer spending and economic growth, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term (PAYEMS * RSAFS) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth rate above 3.0% during a late-cycle expansion signals potential overheating and the likelihood of monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods classified as late-cycle expansion, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases when GDP growth exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the GDPC1 signal in this regime is below 0.03.
